walkthroughs.body_html: The South China Sea carries ~$3.4 trillion in annual trade and holds estimated reserves of 11 billion barrels of oil. China's nine-dash line claims ~90% of the sea, contested by Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei. In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled against China under UNCLOS, but China rejected the ruling and continues island-building on Mischief Reef and Fiery Cross Reef.

Beginning in 2018, the Trump administration imposed tariffs on ~$370bn of Chinese goods, citing IP theft and forced technology transfer. China retaliated on $110bn of US exports. The decoupling agenda continued under Biden with CHIPS Act restrictions on semiconductor exports to China. Supply chains shifted toward Vietnam, Mexico and India, a process termed friend-shoring.

Advanced chips have become the new strategic chokepoint. The USA restricts ASML EUV lithography exports to China, while TSMC (Taiwan) produces ~90% of leading-edge chips, making Taiwan a critical flashpoint. This tech containment mirrors Cold War strategy, with allies (Japan, Netherlands, South Korea) coordinating export controls under the Chip 4 alliance.
